response.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) AS average_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) AS total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: The database system supports PostgreSQL-style NULLS LAST syntax in ORDER BY clauses. Other databases (MySQL, SQLite, etc.) use different syntax for explicit NULL ordering.

alternatives.interpretation: If 'ignoring missing values' means to exclude fee records with NULL rebrate or rebtotal entirely before grouping (rather than just from the aggregates), add filtering conditions to the WHERE clause.
alternatives.sql: SELECT f.orderslink, o.mktnote, AVG(f.rebrate) AS average_rebrate, SUM(f.rebtotal) AS total_rebate FROM fees f INNER JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate >= 0.0009 AND f.rebrate IS NOT NULL AND f.rebtotal IS NOT NULL GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.mktnote ORDER BY total_rebate DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
